content.raw_text: 一天下午，海生对一个朋友说：“你中午没吃饭，你想去我家的饭店吗？我爸爸做的面很好吃！”

sentences.text: 一天下午，海生对一个朋友说：“你中午没吃饭，你想去我家的饭店吗？
sentences.translation: One afternoon, Haisheng said to a friend, "You didn't have lunch, do you want to go to my family's restaurant?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject-Verb-Object. The use of "没" indicates the negative past tense, meaning "did not have". The question particle "吗" is used at the end to turn the sentence into a question.

sentences.translation: My dad's noodles are very delicious!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Possessive Particle + Object + Adjective. The word '的' is used to indicate possession in this context.
The sentence contains opening and closing quotation marks.

content.raw_text: “好！”朋友开心地说。

sentences.translation: Good!
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple exclamation expressing approval or satisfaction.

sentences.translation: The friend said happily.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Adverb + Verb, which is a common pattern in Chinese sentences.

content.raw_text: 他们一边走一边说话。走到店门边的时候，海生看到饭店关门了。

sentences.translation: They walk and talk at the same time.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一边...一边...' is used to indicate simultaneous actions happening at the same time.

sentences.text: 走到店门边的时候，海生看到饭店关门了。
sentences.translation: When he walked to the door of the shop, Haisheng saw that the restaurant was closed.
sentences.explanation: The structure '看到' means 'saw' in this context. '了' is a particle indicating completion of an action.

content.raw_text: 海生想：“怎么会关门呢？还不到五点。”

sentences.translation: Hai Sheng thought: 'How could it be closed?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a question expressing surprise or disbelief.

words.definition: modal particle indicating a rhetorical question

sentences.translation: It's not even five o'clock yet.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Time + Verb. In this sentence, the time '五点' (five o'clock) is the main focus, and the word order is 'not even five o'clock yet.'
This sentence only consists of a closing quotation mark and a space, with no actual text content.

content.raw_text: 海生又说：“妈妈，我回来了！”没有人说话。

sentences.text: 海生又说：“妈妈，我回来了！
sentences.translation: Hai Sheng said, 'Mom, I'm back!'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The particle '了' indicates the completion of the action of coming back.

sentences.translation: No one spoke.
sentences.explanation: The structure '没有人' means 'no one' in Chinese, and the verb '说话' means 'to speak' or 'to talk'.

content.raw_text: “爸爸，我朋友想吃面。”还是没有人说话。

sentences.translation: Dad, my friend wants to eat noodles.
sentences.explanation: The structure '想吃' means 'wants to eat' in this context. The word '面' specifically refers to noodles in this sentence.

sentences.translation: Still, no one spoke.
sentences.explanation: The structure '还是' is used to express 'still' in this context, indicating that despite the situation, no one spoke.

content.raw_text: 老周和周太太都不在，饭店里一个人也没有，可是店门也没关好。

sentences.text: 老周和周太太都不在，饭店里一个人也没有，可是店门也没关好。
sentences.translation: Mr. Zhou and Mrs. Zhou are not here, there is no one in the restaurant, but the door is not closed properly.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the absence of Mr. and Mrs. Zhou in the restaurant, emphasizing that even though there is no one inside, the door is not properly closed.

content.raw_text: 海生的朋友看看他，说：“你爸爸不在，我明天再来吃面吧。”

sentences.text: 海生的朋友看看他，说：“你爸爸不在，我明天再来吃面吧。
sentences.translation: Hai's friend looked at him and said, 'Your dad is not here, I will come again tomorrow to eat noodles.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains possessive particle '的' and a modal particle '吧', which are common in Chinese grammar.

words.definition: modal particle indicating suggestion or request

sentences.explanation: The sentence is incomplete and only contains a closing quotation mark and a space.

content.raw_text: “不行，我们都来了，吃吧！”海生说，“我爸爸不在，我来给你做。”说完，海生对朋友笑笑。

sentences.translation: No, we all came, let's eat!
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses the particle '都' to emphasize that everyone has arrived. The final '吧' is a suggestive particle indicating a suggestion or proposal.

sentences.text: ”海生说，“我爸爸不在，我来给你做。
sentences.translation: Hai Sheng said, "My dad is not here, I will cook for you."
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The use of "给" indicates the action is done for someone else.

sentences.translation: After speaking, Haisheng smiled at his friend.
sentences.explanation: In Chinese, reduplication of a verb can indicate a light or gentle action. In this case, the reduplication of the verb "笑" (smile) indicates a gentle or friendly smile.

content.raw_text: “你也会做面？”朋友也笑笑，“我要看看你是怎么做的。”

sentences.translation: Do you know how to make noodles?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a question asking if the person knows how to make noodles. The character '会' in this context indicates the ability or skill to do something.

sentences.text: ”朋友也笑笑，“我要看看你是怎么做的。
sentences.translation: My friend also smiled, 'I want to see how you do it.'
sentences.explanation: The repetition of '看看' emphasizes the action of 'seeing' in this context. The particle '的' at the end of the sentence indicates the completion of the action of 'doing'.

words.definition: particle indicating completion of an action

sentences.explanation: This sentence only contains a closing quotation mark and a space.

content.raw_text: “我小时候天天看我爸爸做面，也跟他学了一点。”海生一边跟朋友说话，一边做面。面做完了以后，他和朋友都很开心。

sentences.text: “我小时候天天看我爸爸做面，也跟他学了一点。
sentences.translation: When I was young, I watched my dad make noodles every day, and I also learned a little from him.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes the speaker's childhood experience of watching and learning how to make noodles from their father.

sentences.text: ”海生一边跟朋友说话，一边做面。
sentences.translation: Hai Sheng makes noodles while talking to his friend.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一边...一边...' is used to express doing two actions simultaneously. In this sentence, Hai Sheng is making noodles and talking to his friend at the same time.

sentences.text: 面做完了以后，他和朋友都很开心。
sentences.translation: After making the noodles, he and his friends were very happy.
sentences.explanation: The structure '...以后' means 'after ...' in this context. Also, '都' is used to indicate 'both' in this sentence.

content.raw_text: “怎么样？好吃吗？”海生一边吃，一边问朋友。

sentences.translation: How is it?
sentences.explanation: The phrase 怎么样 is commonly used to ask for someone's opinion or feedback on something.

sentences.translation: Is it delicious?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Question Particle, where 吗 is used at the end to turn a statement into a yes-no question.

sentences.translation: Hai Sheng eats while asking his friend.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一边...一边...' is used to indicate simultaneous actions happening at the same time.

content.raw_text: “好吃，太好吃了！”

sentences.translation: Delicious, so delicious!
sentences.explanation: The structure '太 + adjective + 了' is used to express 'too + adjective'. In this sentence, the speaker is emphasizing how delicious the food is.

words.definition: Indicates completion or change of state

sentences.explanation: This sentence only consists of a closing quotation mark and a space.

content.raw_text: “那你多吃点！”海生开心地说。

sentences.translation: Eat more!
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple command telling someone to eat more. The word '点' here is used to soften the command, making it more polite.

sentences.translation: Hai Sheng said happily.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern of Subject + Adverb + Verb. The adverbial particle '地' is used to modify the verb '说' (said).

content.raw_text: “谢谢，我吃完了。”朋友很开心，“可是，我没有钱。多少钱？我明天给你。”

sentences.translation: Thank you, I finished eating.
sentences.explanation: The structure '吃完了' means 'finished eating' in this context. The particle '了' indicates the completion of the action.

sentences.translation: The friend is very happy, but I have no money.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is simple, with the conjunction '可是' (but) used to contrast the friend's happiness with the speaker's lack of money.

sentences.translation: How much?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple question asking about the price of something. '多少' means 'how much' and '钱' means 'money'.

sentences.translation: I will give it to you tomorrow.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object, where the subject '我' (I) is followed by the verb '给' (give) and then the object '你' (you). The time indicator '明天' (tomorrow) is placed before the verb to indicate when the action will happen.
This sentence only consists of a closing quotation mark and a space, with no actual content.

content.raw_text: “今天的面不要钱。”海生说完以后他们都笑了。

sentences.translation: Today's noodles are free.
sentences.explanation: The tricky part here is the use of '的' as a possessive particle to indicate that the noodles belong to today, meaning 'today's noodles'. Also, '不要' can be translated as 'do not want' or 'do not need' depending on the context.

words.definition: do not want / do not need

sentences.translation: After Haisheng finished speaking, they all laughed.
sentences.explanation: The structure '说完以后' means 'finished speaking and then'. The use of '都' emphasizes that everyone laughed.

content.raw_text: 这时候，来了几个人，想吃饭和菜。

sentences.text: 这时候，来了几个人，想吃饭和菜。
sentences.translation: At this time, a few people came, wanting to eat rice and dishes.
sentences.explanation: The structure '想吃' means 'wanting to eat'. In Chinese, the verb '吃' (to eat) is often followed by another verb to indicate the action one wants to do.

content.raw_text: “我爸爸妈妈出去了，我不会做菜。你们晚上再来吧。”海生对那几个人说。

sentences.text: “我爸爸妈妈出去了，我不会做菜。
sentences.translation: My parents went out, I can't cook.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不会' is used to indicate inability or lack of skill in doing something.

sentences.translation: Come back again at night.
sentences.explanation: The word '吧' at the end of the sentence is used to soften the command and make it sound more like a suggestion or invitation.

sentences.translation: Hai Sheng said to those few people.
sentences.explanation: The structure '对...说' is a common way to express 'said to' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: “那你们吃的是什么？”一个男人一边笑一边问。

sentences.translation: What are you guys eating?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. In this sentence, the subject is '你们' (you guys), the verb is '吃' (eat), and the object is '什么' (what). The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association.

sentences.translation: A man asked while smiling.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一边...一边...' is used to indicate simultaneous actions happening at the same time.

content.raw_text: “面，他做的。”海生的朋友说。

sentences.translation: Noodles, he made.
sentences.explanation: This sentence follows the Subject-Verb-Object word order commonly used in Chinese. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate that the noodles were made by him.

sentences.translation: Hai's friend said.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Possessive Particle + Noun + Verb, which is common in Chinese. The possessive particle '的' indicates possession or relationship between 'Hai' and 'friend'.

content.raw_text: “好吃吗？”男人又问。

sentences.translation: Is it delicious?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Question Particle, where the question particle 吗 is added at the end to turn a statement into a yes-no question.

sentences.translation: The man asked again.
sentences.explanation: The word "又" is used to indicate the action is happening again, adding emphasis to the repetition.

content.raw_text: “很好吃。”海生的朋友开心地说。

sentences.translation: Very delicious.
sentences.explanation: The structure '很 + adjective' is commonly used in Chinese to express a high degree of the adjective, in this case, '很好吃' means 'very delicious'.

sentences.translation: Hai's friend said happily.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern Subject + Possessive Particle + Noun + Adjective + Adverbial Particle + Verb.

content.raw_text: 几个男人又笑了：“好，那我们今天也吃面。去做吧。”

sentences.text: 几个男人又笑了：“好，那我们今天也吃面。
sentences.translation: Several men laughed again: 'Alright, then let's have noodles today too.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, but the use of '又' (again) indicates a repeated action, and '也' (too) emphasizes the inclusion of noodles in their meal for that day.

sentences.translation: Go do it.
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple command or suggestion, asking someone to go and do something.

words.definition: modal particle indicating suggestion or urging

sentences.explanation: This sentence only contains a closing quotation mark and a space, with no actual text content.

content.raw_text: 海生想，要是爸爸知道了会生气。可是，他也很开心：这是他第一次在饭店里做面！

sentences.text: 海生想，要是爸爸知道了会生气。
sentences.translation: Hai Sheng thought, if dad knew, he would be angry.
sentences.explanation: The structure '要是...会...' is used to express a hypothetical situation or a conditional statement in Chinese.

sentences.text: 可是，他也很开心：这是他第一次在饭店里做面！
sentences.translation: However, he was also very happy: this was the first time he made noodles in a restaurant!
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the concept of making noodles in a restaurant for the first time, highlighting the character's happiness.

content.raw_text: “小朋友，我喜欢你的面。”吃完面，一个男人对海生说。“多少钱？”

sentences.translation: Little child, I like your noodles.
sentences.explanation: The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association between '你' (you) and '面' (noodles).

sentences.translation: After finishing the noodles, a man said to Haisheng.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject-Verb-Object. The character 海生 (Haisheng) is a name.

sentences.translation: How much?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple question asking about the price of something. The word '多少' means 'how much' and '钱' means 'money'.
The sentence contains opening and closing quotation marks, indicating a direct quote or specific text being referenced.

content.raw_text: “我不知道……”海生看看那个男人，笑了：“给多少都行。”

sentences.translation: I don't know...
sentences.explanation: The sentence starts with an opening quotation mark and is followed by the pronoun 'I', the negation 'not', the verb 'know', and an ellipsis indicating an unfinished thought.

sentences.text: ”海生看看那个男人，笑了：“给多少都行。
sentences.translation: Hai Sheng looked at the man and smiled: 'Any amount will do.'
sentences.explanation: The structure '给多少都行' means 'any amount will do' in this context. The use of '给' (give) followed by '多少' (how much) and '都' (all) is a common way to express 'any amount' in Chinese.
This sentence only consists of a closing quotation mark and a space, with no actual content.

content.raw_text: “我们会再来的。”给了钱，几个男人走了出去。

sentences.translation: We will come again.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is subject-verb-object, with the particle '的' used at the end for emphasis or completion.

sentences.translation: Gave money, several men walked out.
sentences.explanation: The structure 几个 (several) is used to indicate an approximate number of people in this context.

content.raw_text: 过了一会儿，又来了几个人。海生又做了面，大家都很喜欢吃他做的面。可是，吃完以后，每个人给的钱都不一样，谁都不知道要给多少钱。

sentences.text: 过了一会儿，又来了几个人。
sentences.translation: After a while, several more people came.
sentences.explanation: The structure '又...了' indicates a repeated action, in this case, more people coming after a while.

sentences.text: 海生又做了面，大家都很喜欢吃他做的面。
sentences.translation: Haisheng made noodles again, everyone really likes to eat the noodles he made.
sentences.explanation: The structure '大家都很喜欢' means 'everyone really likes'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate that the noodles were made by 'him'.

sentences.text: 可是，吃完以后，每个人给的钱都不一样，谁都不知道要给多少钱。
sentences.translation: However, after eating, everyone gave different amounts of money, and no one knew how much to give.
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains the structure '谁都不知道' which means 'no one knew'. The use of '都' emphasizes that each person was in the same situation of not knowing.
